---
title: The API reference
description: Reference pages made from your code, and names in backticks that link to them.
order: 5
---

smalldocs writes a reference page for each module of your package. A reference page lists the classes
and the functions of a module, with their parameters. smalldocs reads what the code already says, so
you write nothing twice:

- The types come from the annotations.
- The description of each parameter comes from the comment beside it.
- The summary comes from the docstring.

The [Reference](../api/site.qmd) of this site is made from the code of smalldocs in this way.

## Write the code

Put one parameter on each line, with its comment beside it. Put the comment for the return value after
the colon of the `def` line. [fastcore](https://fastcore.fast.ai) calls these comments docments.

```python
def add(
    a: int,  # The first number
    b: int = 2,  # The second number
) -> int:  # Their sum
    "Add two numbers."
    return a + b
```

smalldocs shows other kinds of class in their own way:

- A dataclass shows its constructor, with the comment beside each field.
- A pydantic model shows its fields, with their descriptions.
- A `TypedDict` shows its keys, with the comment beside each key.

## Turn on the reference

Add a `smalldocs.api` section to `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
smalldocs:
  api:
    packages: [mypkg]                  # the importable packages to document
    out: api                           # the folder of pages, inside the site; `api` by default
    root: ..                           # the root of the repository, from the folder of the site
    source: https://github.com/me/mypkg/blob/main   # each entry links to its line here
    check: ["*.py", "tests/**/*.py"]   # more files that `smalldocs api check` holds to the convention
```

The default `root` is `..`. If the folder of the site holds `pyproject.toml`, the default is `.`.

Each build then writes a page `api/<module>.qmd` for each public module. It also writes
`_symbols.json`, the index of names. The folder `out` must be inside the site.

smalldocs notes the pages that it writes in the file `api/.smalldocs-api`. It deletes a page only if an
earlier build wrote the page and the new build did not. So a page of your own in the folder, such as
`api/index.qmd`, is safe.

To list the pages in the sidebar, use a glob:

```yaml
website:
  sidebar:
    contents:
      - section: Reference
        contents: api/*
```

smalldocs imports your package. So install smalldocs in the environment of the package. If the import
fails, smalldocs also looks in the root of the repository and in its `src` folder.

## Links from the text

When the reference is on, a name in backticks becomes a link to its entry, on every page of the site.
The name must be in the reference, for example `Site`, `inventory` or `smalldocs.markdown.render`. A name
inside a link stays as it is. A name that the reference does not know stays as code.

## Use the reference at the terminal

```bash
smalldocs api build --dir docs        # write the pages and the index
smalldocs api module site --dir docs  # print one module as Markdown, for people and agents
smalldocs api list --dir docs         # every module, class, method and function, one line each
smalldocs api check --dir docs        # what is typed and documented, and every gap; exit 1 if any
```

`check` reports each gap in the code:

- a function without a docstring
- a parameter without a type or a docment
- a return value without a type or a docment

Run `check` in your tests, or before each commit.

## Move from apidocs.py

Some projects made their reference with their own `apidocs.py` script and the Lua filter
`linkify.lua`. smalldocs builds such a project with no change:

- smalldocs runs the `pre-render` script. So `apidocs.py` writes the pages and `_symbols.json` as
  before.
- smalldocs sees `linkify.lua` in `filters`, and turns on its own linkify. It does not run the Lua
  file. See [Linkify](config.qmd#linkify).

To change to `smalldocs.api`, do these steps:

1. Add the section above to `_quarto.yml`. Linkify is then on, with no filter.
2. Remove `apidocs.py` from `pre-render`. Keep the other scripts of `pre-render`.
3. Remove `linkify.lua` from `filters`, and remove `symbols` from the section `smalldocs`.
4. Delete the files `apidocs.py` and `linkify.lua`.
5. Delete the old pages in the reference folder, once. smalldocs deletes only the pages that it wrote.

For the `apidocs.py` of babykev, the pages that smalldocs writes are the same, byte for byte.
